name: Baponi

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Credits: $1/1,000 excess credits on Pro after 10,000 included. No confirmed independent RAM/CPU coefficients.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Annual subscription, sales-quoted by deployment scope and support; self-hosted in the customer's Kubernetes/VPC. Unlimited executions, users and API keys; no per-execution metering, credit system or usage caps.

caveats: Public credit-metered execution, not per-second CPU/RAM product. One credit covers 60s at 1 CPU+1 GiB; larger matched CPU/RAM sizes scale credits linearly (2 CPU/2 GiB is 2 credits/minute). Separate CPU×RAM multiplication would be wrong.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Streaming/async output requires Pro. Free: 5 concurrent, 1 custom OCI image, 10 API keys. Concurrency limit returns HTTP 429. One execution per thread_id at a time (409).
Thread state retention is configurable (24 h, 7 d, 30 d, forever default) and counts toward the 10 GB free storage then $0.10/GB-month.

fleet.verification: Free developer documentation explicitly says no credit card. Paid-plan payment/identity checks not detailed.
fleet.tiers: Free 5 concurrent runs; Pro 100; Enterprise advertises unlimited (sales).
fleet.notes: Concurrency counts executions, not retained machines. 10/50 runs fit Pro; 300/1,000 require Enterprise discussion. Separate vCPU/GPU account quotas and turnaround unknown.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Execution finishes. The sandbox state is snapshotted and the sandbox is destroyed. Billing stops.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: end of every execution that carries a thread_id; next call with the same thread_id restores it. Filesystem only: the diff of /home/baponi (not /tmp, no memory/processes: 'Between these calls, nothing is running ... It's a saved filesystem state' - how-it-works). Retention 24h/7d/30d/forever, billed as storage beyond 10 GB free.

harness_api.quote: "code": "claude -p \"Research the current price of Bitcoin and summarize your findings\" --dangerously-skip-permissions",
harness_api.note: Claude Code is run through the generic /v1/sandbox/execute endpoint (bash command, --output-format stream-json parsed by you). No first-party harness API (no prompt/session/follow-up endpoints). Claude Code appears preinstalled (/home/baponi/.local/bin/claude) -> agent_harnesses, not harness_api.

egress_allowlist.quote: **Blocked** (default): No network interface at all. No DNS, no outbound connections.
egress_allowlist.note: Binary policy only: 'blocked' (default, no network interface) or 'unrestricted'; set per sandbox config, API key can downgrade unrestricted->blocked but never the reverse. 'Internal networks (private IPs, cloud metadata endpoints) are always blocked at the network layer.' No per-domain or per-IP allow/deny list documented, hence level null. Enforced outside the nsjail (per-sandbox network namespace).

ingress_rules.note: Not applicable in practice: sandboxes are per-call (spin up, execute, tear down) and there is no port exposure / preview URL / inbound feature anywhere in the docs or API endpoint list, so nothing inbound to control. Card: inbound_https=false.

guest_firewall.quote: nsjail enforces Linux namespace isolation with a strict seccomp-bpf syscall allowlist, cgroups v2 resource control, zero Linux capabilities, and per-sandbox network namespaces.
guest_firewall.note: nsjail container with zero capabilities (no CAP_NET_ADMIN), non-root user baponi; cannot run iptables/nftables.

secret_proxy.quote: Baponi injects the credentials as standard config files that CLI tools expect
secret_proxy.note: Connectors (PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Redis, MongoDB, S3, GCS, Azure, GitHub, Anthropic) inject the real secret INTO the sandbox as RAM-mounted config files/env vars (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var, GH_TOKEN, .pgpass), wiped after execution - the code can read them, so not a proxy. Exception: BYOB bucket credentials stay in a separate mount process ('never inside the sandbox'), but that is a storage mount, not an HTTP credential proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Baponi gives every organization storage that works exactly like BYOB, with the first 10 GB free and expandable as you grow.
volume_attach.note: Managed volumes (Baponi-hosted, $0.10/GB-mo beyond 10 GB) and BYOB S3/GCS/Azure buckets mounted at /data/{slug}/ on every execution; object-storage-backed FUSE-style mounts, not block volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Shared across API keys in the organization
volume_shared.note: Volumes/BYOB buckets mount into every sandbox of the org (per-key path scoping); many concurrent executions see the same bucket. Access mode 'Read-write or read-only (configurable)'. Writes sync back before the execution response returns (consistency across concurrent writers not documented).

desktop.quote: A sandbox platform built from the ground up for AI agent workloads... Every call gets a fresh sandbox in under 20ms, torn down when execution ends.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Baponi is a stateless code-execution API (Python/Node/Bash in an nsjail sandbox), not a GUI/VM product; no VNC/RDP/stream desktop is documented.

browser.quote: Welcome to the Baponi developer documentation... Full reference for the Execute, Files, and MCP endpoints.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser runtime, browser connector, or browser automation is listed among connectors (databases, storage, GitHub, Anthropic) or docs.

computer_use.quote: A sandbox platform built from the ground up for AI agent workloads
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no desktop, so no screenshot+click driving API exists.

anti_bot.quote: With Baponi, you choose per sandbox: `blocked` (default) or `unrestricted` (full outbound internet).
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a code-execution sandbox with a binary network policy, no browser/stealth fingerprinting feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Baponi is a sandboxed code execution platform for AI agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving feature or connector exists; product is code execution, not a browser/scraping agent.

ssh.quote: Baponi is a sandboxed code execution platform for AI agents. You send code, it runs in an isolated sandbox... One HTTP call.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes are ephemeral, created per API call and torn down after execution (sub-20ms boot); there is no persistent addressable machine to SSH into, and no SSH access is documented anywhere in the API/docs.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Execution finishes. The sandbox state is snapshotted and the sandbox is destroyed. Billing stops.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Snapshotting is automatic on every execution end (tied to thread_id), not a separate on-demand snapshot API/CLI call the user can invoke at will.

fork.quote: Next call with the same thread\_id restores the snapshot. Hours, days, or weeks later.
fork.note: Only one thread_id restores to its own single snapshot lineage; no documented API to clone a thread's state into a new, independent thread/sandbox.

fork_running.quote: Execution finishes. The sandbox state is snapshotted and the sandbox is destroyed.
fork_running.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes are always destroyed between calls (never kept running), and fork is not offered at all, so cloning a running machine is impossible by design.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: It's a saved filesystem state... Between these calls, nothing is running.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots are filesystem-only (no memory/process state), and fork is not offered, so memory-preserving forks are not possible.

pause_resume.quote: Execution finishes. The sandbox state is snapshotted and the sandbox is destroyed. Billing stops.
pause_resume.note: There is no running machine to pause — every execution fully tears down the sandbox and billing stops entirely; resuming via thread_id recreates a fresh sandbox from the filesystem snapshot rather than pausing/unpausing an existing one.

wake_on_request.quote: Next call with the same thread_id restores the snapshot. Hours, days, or weeks later. The agent never manages container lifecycle.
wake_on_request.note: Every API call automatically spins up a fresh sandbox (restoring prior state if thread_id matches) with no explicit start/wake call needed.

persistent_disk.quote: Stateful when you need it. Pass a thread_id to persist state across calls. Installed packages, environment variables, and filesystem changes survive between executions, even across days or weeks.

live_resize.quote: Each API key is bound to: A sandbox (runtime image, CPU, RAM, network policy)
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are fixed per API key/sandbox config set in the admin console; each execution is a brand-new sandbox instance, so there is no running machine whose resources get resized live.

agent_harnesses.quote: Run Claude Code as a remote headless agent inside an isolated Baponi sandbox. Credentials for Anthropic and GitHub are injected automatically through connectors.
agent_harnesses.note: Claude Code is preinstalled/documented as a guided integration (run via bash execute calls), qualifying as an offered coding-agent harness even though it's driven through the generic execute endpoint rather than a dedicated harness API.

own_agent_api.quote: Baponi is a sandboxed code execution platform for AI agents. Authenticate with an API key, send code, get results.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Baponi provides a code-execution API only; it does not ship its own browser/computer-use/research task agent to drive.

public_ipv4.quote: With Baponi, you choose per sandbox: `blocked` (default) or `unrestricted` (full outbound internet).
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes only support outbound network access when unrestricted; there is no inbound HTTPS/port exposure or per-machine public IPv4 documented anywhere in the API/docs.

egress_http_rules.quote: **Blocked** (default): No network interface at all. No DNS, no outbound connections.
egress_http_rules.note: Network policy is a binary per-sandbox choice (blocked vs unrestricted); no per-domain, per-IP, or HTTP method/path level egress rule is documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: With Baponi, you choose per sandbox: `blocked` (default) or `unrestricted` (full outbound internet).
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP is documented; each execution runs in a fresh sandbox with no addressed egress IP guarantee mentioned.

gpu.quote: Max CPU per sandbox | 1 core | 4 cores | Unlimited
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — plan limits table only lists CPU/RAM tiers; no GPU option is offered anywhere in pricing or docs.

windows.quote: You send code, it runs in an isolated sandbox with multi-layer security... Built on Google's nsjail.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes are Linux nsjail containers; Windows machines are not offered.

macos.quote: Built on Google's nsjail. Six independent isolation layers enforced at the kernel level.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Linux nsjail-based container sandboxes only; no macOS machines offered.

open_source.quote: Or skip our cloud and run it all in your VPC with one Helm chart. Your infra, your rules.
open_source.note: Self-hosting is offered via a distributed Helm chart (byoc-style deployment into the customer's own Kubernetes/VPC), but no OSI license or public source repository is named; core platform appears closed-source, distributed as a deployable chart/image.

docker_inside.quote: Sandboxes run with zero Linux capabilities. No CAP_NET_RAW, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no CAP_SYS_PTRACE. There is nothing to escalate to because nothing was granted. ... Runs as unprivileged UID 1000, zero capabilities, user namespaces disabled.
docker_inside.note: Docker-in-sandbox requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN and/or user namespaces to create containers; Baponi explicitly drops all capabilities and disables user namespaces, and no docs anywhere mention a docker/containerd binary being available inside the nsjail sandbox. No is confirmed.

nested_virt.quote: Sandbox boundaries powered by hardened nsjail. ... Capability Dropping: Sandboxes run with zero Linux capabilities.
nested_virt.note: Isolation is nsjail (Linux namespaces + seccomp-bpf + cgroups v2), not a hypervisor/microVM; no KVM/virtualization device is exposed and capabilities (needed for /dev/kvm access) are fully dropped. No mention anywhere in docs/features/trust pages of nested virtualization support. No is confirmed.

root.quote: Cannot escalate privileges. Runs as unprivileged UID 1000, zero capabilities, user namespaces disabled.
root.note: Explicit statement that sandbox code runs as unprivileged UID 1000 with zero Linux capabilities. No is confirmed.

inbound_https.quote: With Baponi, you choose per sandbox: blocked (default) or unrestricted (full outbound internet).
inbound_https.note: Network policy is described only in outbound terms (blocked vs unrestricted egress); there is no port-exposure, preview-URL, ingress, or inbound-HTTPS feature anywhere in the docs, API reference (POST /v1/sandbox/execute is the only network-relevant endpoint), features page, or trust center. No is confirmed.

soc2.quote: Audit logging on every tier. SOC 2 Type 1 preparation kickoff Q4 2026. Enterprise security controls available today. Formal certifications in progress. ... In Progress: SOC 2 Type 1, Preparation kickoff Q4 2026
soc2.note: Trust center explicitly lists SOC 2 Type 1 as 'In Progress' with prep starting Q4 2026, i.e. not certified as of 2026-09-30. No is confirmed. (Audit logging is described as 'SOC 2-grade' but that is not a certification.)

hipaa.quote: Enterprise deployments inherit your existing compliance posture. Self-hosted Baponi runs inside your certified infrastructure. Your SOC 2, your HIPAA, your FedRAMP - Baponi operates within the controls you've already established.
hipaa.note: Baponi has no HIPAA certification or BAA offering of its own; HIPAA compliance is only achievable by self-hosting inside the customer's already-compliant infrastructure ('your HIPAA'). No HIPAA/BAA mention anywhere else on pricing, features, or trust pages. No is confirmed.
